contract.words: Collect $7,500 of settled cash within 45 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $7,500 of settled cash collected within 45 days

strategy.title: No plan yet: facade-grant application packets have no established purchase price
strategy.why: Buyers (85 eligible buildings, county assessor mailing addresses), current demand (posted 2026-11-24), conversion (4 of 40 measured on this offer), fulfilment (a spreadsheet Brain produces, $20 direct cost) and settlement (10 days) are evidenced, but the card's only price figure, $7,500, is the city grant award a building owner may receive, not a fee any owner is shown to pay for an application packet. A grant is not a purchase price, so the offer's price, and therefore how many deals the $7,500 target needs, is not established.

alternatives.title: Sell packets at $7,500 each, one deal reaching the target
alternatives.why: Rejected: $7,500 is the maximum grant award (city program page), not what owners pay a preparer; no owner is shown paying it, and charging the whole award for the application is not an evidenced price.

alternatives.title: Conditional outreach at an assumed fee
alternatives.why: Rejected: the fee buyers pay is a published-market question research can answer first; a guessed fee also leaves the deal count, and whether 85 eligible owners at a 10% close rate can carry $7,500, undecided.

noPlan.decisiveGap: OFFER_AND_PRICE: no price that a building owner pays for a facade-grant application packet is established; the only figure on the card ($7,500) is the grant award ceiling, which is money the city pays the owner, not a purchase price.
noPlan.resolution: Research published fees for preparing facade-improvement / historic-preservation grant applications (grant-writer and consultant fee schedules, sourced and dated, for building owners). With an established fee F, the 85 eligible owners at the measured 10% close rate give about 8 deals; re-plan if 8 x F (or a repeatable fee structure) reaches $7,500 settled inside 45 days, otherwise report the target as out of reach on established figures.

facts.value: 85 buildings in the downtown historic district are eligible; the grant round is open until 2027-01-15.
Sell Facade-improvement grant application packets for historic-district building owners to each buyer.
The city's Facade Improvement Grant program awards up to $7,500 to downtown historic-district building owners for exterior restoration work (city program page, 2026-10).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance. The only price fact on the card is the city's facade grant award ceiling ($7,500) - money the city pays the owner, not a fee any owner is shown paying for an application packet - so OFFER_AND_PRICE is genuinely unestablished and is correctly named as the decisive link. Every other link (reachable buyer via assessor mailing addresses, signal dated 2026-11-24, 4/40 measured conversion, Brain-produced spreadsheet at $20, 10-day settlement in a 45-day window, $0 exposure) is evidenced on the card. Without a price the deal count is undetermined, so no executable or conditional plan can be sized.
findings: $7,500 is a grant award (city -> owner), not a purchase price; treating it as price would make one deal = target, which the plan correctly rejects.
Arithmetic in resolution checks: 85 eligible x 10% measured close = ~8.5 deals, so a fee of at least ~$940/packet would be needed to reach $7,500; the re-plan rule is stated correctly.
No money is committed and the single research step costs $0, inside the $0 exposure cap.
Minor: conversion 4/40 was measured without an established price, so it should be re-checked once a fee is found - not decisive now.
